per_plume.source_hint: south of Hawaii Island, tracked source end ~58 km south of Kilauea summit; Kilauea degassing possible but unconfirmed
evidence: Kilauea WATCH/ORANGE with small north-vent overflows for fourth day and strong glow, plus 43 Kilauea-summit thermal pixels; Mauna Loa NORMAL/GREEN not erupting, so if volcanic the source would be Kilauea, not Mauna Loa. [E1, E6]

114-km streak south of Hawaii Island with centroid 48.1 km from Kilauea and tracked southern source end 58.4 km south of Kilauea; ENE wind from 72 deg at 15.1 kmh (blowing toward ~252 deg WSW) makes a south-of-island location broadly plausible for vog transport but offset is large. [E2, E3, E5]

Measured drift toward 31 deg NNE at 5.2 kmh disagrees with wind-implied transport toward ~252 deg WSW by ~139 deg, with poor fit R2 0.33 and speed much slower than wind, contradicting the trade-wind transport story and lowering confidence. [E2, E5]

Mask land_frac 1.0 covering 20.7% of Hawaii Island and described as faint dark gray over bright white clouds in mostly cloudy scene indicates land/cloud contamination, not a clear over-water plume; FIRMS shows no fire clusters to support wildfire smoke. [E4, E6]

kilauea.activity_summary: Small overflows from the north vent continue for the fourth day. All vents have strong glow, with overflows and intermittent spatter from the north vent. There is no anomalous activity outside of the summit.

mauna_loa.activity_summary: Mauna Loa earthquake counts increased in August, while the summit region showed no other signs of deformation. Mauna Loa had an increase in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 87 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the August reporting period, after 57 in July. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks.
